label: Schemes, coverages, formations, situations, outcomes and counters
definition: The scheme layer: how teams organise, which ball-screen coverage they play, when a scheme is used, what it is designed to produce, and the tactical answers to it.

nodes.label: Half-court
nodes.definition: A set defence is in place and the offence must generate a shot against it.

nodes.label: Transition
nodes.definition: Possession immediately after a change of possession, before the defence can set its shell.

nodes.label: Early offence
nodes.definition: The first 4-8 seconds: pushing the ball to get a shot before the defence organises, or to flow straight into a set.

nodes.label: Late shot clock
nodes.definition: Under ~8 seconds on the shot clock: no time for a second action, one read only.

nodes.label: Sideline out of bounds (SLOB)
nodes.definition: Inbounding from the sideline; the defence can trap the passer or deny the first option.

nodes.label: Baseline out of bounds (BLOB)
nodes.definition: Inbounding under the offensive basket; the defence must guard the rim and the arc at once.

nodes.label: After timeout (ATO)
nodes.definition: A scripted play run out of a stoppage, with a designed first and second option.

nodes.label: Clutch
nodes.definition: The last five minutes with a margin of five points or fewer.

nodes.label: Scramble / broken play
nodes.definition: The called play has broken down; players must play out of rules and spacing rather than script.

nodes.label: Against a press
nodes.definition: The defence is applying full-court or three-quarter-court pressure.

nodes.label: 5-Out
nodes.definition: All five players start outside the arc; the lane is empty and the rim protector must defend in space.

nodes.label: 4-Out-1-In
nodes.definition: Four perimeter players plus one big on the block or the dunker spot; keeps a rim threat while spacing the arc.

nodes.label: Horns
nodes.definition: Two bigs at the elbows, two shooters in the corners, ball handler at the top; opens pick-and-roll, hand-off and high-low actions.

nodes.label: Box
nodes.definition: Four players in a box across the lane; common BLOB alignment for screens and misdirection.

nodes.label: 2-3 Shell
nodes.definition: Defensive alignment: two perimeter defenders up top, three across the bottom of the zone.

nodes.label: 3-2 Shell
nodes.definition: Defensive alignment: three defenders across the top, two on the back line.

nodes.label: 1-2-1-1 Press
nodes.definition: Full-court press alignment: one at the ball, two at the first trap line, one at mid-court, one deep.

nodes.label: Drop
nodes.definition: The screener's defender sinks well below the screen to protect the rim and dares the ball handler to shoot the pull-up.

props.vulnerability: Open pull-up three for a shot-making ball handler
key: Protects the rim and the defensive glass
Requires a rim protector who can cover ground on the recovery

nodes.label: At the level
nodes.definition: The screener's defender meets the ball at the level of the screen, then recovers with the roll, splitting the difference between drop and blitz.

props.vulnerability: Behind-the-play passes to the roller if the recovery is late
key: The default 'no-easy-answer' coverage
Demands a big who can move his feet in space

nodes.label: Show and recover (hedge)
nodes.definition: The screener's defender steps out to stall the ball handler for a beat, then sprints back to the roller.

props.vulnerability: The short roll: the screener's man is out of position to cover the elbow catch
key: Disrupts the timing of the action without giving up the rim
The weak-side low man must tag the roller on the recovery

nodes.label: Blitz
nodes.definition: Both defenders attack the ball handler off the screen, forcing the ball out of the star's hands.

props.vulnerability: The 4-on-3 behind the trap: a short-roll passer or a hub will dissect it
key: Only works if the back line rotates 'next man up' instantly
Invites a turnover and early offence, or a wide-open corner three

nodes.label: Switch
nodes.definition: The two defenders simply exchange assignments, taking away the pass out of the screen.

props.vulnerability: The mismatch: a smaller defender on a post scorer, or a slow big on a guard in space
key: Removes the first advantage entirely
Requires five players who can hold up in a mismatch, plus scram rotations

nodes.label: ICE (Blue / Down)
nodes.definition: The on-ball defender forces the ball handler towards the baseline, using the sideline as a second defender.

props.vulnerability: The reject: a ball handler who refuses the screen and turns back to the middle
key: Takes away the pull-up and the middle drive
The weak-side defenders must be ready for the kick-out and the reversal

nodes.label: Scram switch
nodes.definition: Not a primary coverage but a repair: after a switch, a third defender swaps onto the mismatch so a guard is never left on a post scorer.

props.vulnerability: The scram itself can be late, leaving a brief open window
key: Turns switch coverage into a full five-man scheme
Communicated before the action, not during it

nodes.label: Pick and Roll (ball screen)
nodes.definition: The organising action of modern basketball: a ball handler and a screener combine against two defenders, and the offence's job is to turn the resulting two-on-two advantage into an advantage for all five.

key: The angle of the screen decides everything: set it on the defender's shoulder, not on his hip
The ball handler must come off shoulder-to-hip, not wide around the screen
The roll is a threat even when it is not passed to: it occupies the rim protector
Spacing is the real weapon: two corner shooters and a weak-side lift punish any rotation
props.note: Treated here both as a scheme (the system) and as the model for play:pick-and-roll (the graph).

nodes.label: Motion Offence
nodes.definition: A rule-based, read-and-react offence: pass, cut, screen away, and fill. There is no fixed play, only a set of principles (pass and cut, fill from the bottom, screen the ball, backdoor the overplay) executed against five moving defenders.

key: Pass and cut: after every pass the passer cuts or screens away
Fill from the bottom: never leave two players in one spot
Backdoor cut when overplayed; basket cut when the defender relaxes
Half-second decisions: catch, read, shoot-pass-drive
Spacing rule: one player in each of the five spots, corners always filled

nodes.label: 5-Out Spacing
nodes.definition: An offensive system in which every player starts beyond the arc, emptying the lane so that drives, hand-offs and rolls happen against a defence with no help at the rim.

key: Removes the rim protector from the play
Demands five players who can shoot, pass and drive a closeout

nodes.label: Spain Pick and Roll
nodes.definition: A ball screen in which a third player sets a back screen on the screener immediately before the ball screen, creating a roll-and-replace action that punishes aggressive coverages.

key: The back screen forces the defence to choose between the ball screen and the slipping screener
The timing is everything: the back screen must land as the ball screen is set

nodes.label: Horns
nodes.definition: A two-big-at-the-elbows set that lets the offence run pick-and-roll, hand-offs, high-low and split action from the same alignment.

key: Same look, four different actions: the defence cannot load up on any one
The corner shooters must stay in the corners to keep the lane clear

nodes.label: Early Offence / Push
nodes.definition: Attacking in the first 4-8 seconds: rim runs, drag screens and early hand-offs before the defence can set its shell.

key: The rim run occupies the back line and creates the corner three
A drag screen in semi-transition catches the defence in cross-matchups

nodes.label: Man-to-Man
nodes.definition: Every defender is responsible for one opponent, plus a defined help position (nail, weak-side low man, back line).

key: On-ball: contain and direct the ball
Off-ball: be in the help position on the flight of the pass, not after it
Every drive is a five-man problem, not a one-man problem

nodes.label: Zone 2-3
nodes.definition: Two defenders across the top and three along the bottom. A paint-protecting shell that concedes the above-the-break three and dares the offence to beat it with passing, patience and rebounding.

key: Move on the flight of the ball: the shell slides with every pass
Touch the midline: weak-side back-line defenders must be in help position
Bump cutters as they pass through your area, then give them up
The top two must 'match' to the ball and take away the middle
Rebounding is the zone's weak point: everyone must find a body

nodes.label: Zone 3-2
nodes.definition: Three defenders across the top, two on the back line; built to bother perimeter shooters and to generate turnovers on the wings.

key: Takes away the above-the-break three
Gives up the corners and the offensive glass: the back two must be elite rebounders

nodes.label: Matchup Zone
nodes.definition: A hybrid that begins in a zone shell but picks up men as they enter each defender's area, combining zone protection with man accountability on the glass.

key: Solves the zone's rebounding problem
Requires five defenders who can communicate and pass off cutters

nodes.label: Pack Line
nodes.definition: A gap-control man-to-man: off-ball defenders sink to a 'line' inside the arc and stunt at the ball, conceding nothing at the rim and forcing tough twos.

key: No middle: every drive is funnelled to a crowded baseline
Vulnerable to a hot shooting night from the arc

nodes.label: Switch-All (Switch Everything)
nodes.definition: Every screen is switched, removing the pass-out advantage and betting on five players who can hold up in any matchup.

key: Takes away the pick-and-roll's first pass and the shooter's window
Concedes the mismatch: it must be answered with scram switches and physical post defence

nodes.label: Full-Court Press
nodes.definition: Applying pressure the length of the floor to burn the eight-second count, force turnovers and dictate tempo.

key: The press is a tempo weapon, not a steal machine: make them use clock
Never let the ball go middle against a trap

nodes.label: Rim attempt
nodes.definition: A shot at or within a step of the basket, the most efficient shot in the game.

nodes.label: Lob dunk
nodes.definition: The highest-percentage finish, produced when the roll man beats the defence to the rim.

nodes.label: Corner three
nodes.definition: The shortest and most efficient three, the classic product of help being forced to the ball.

nodes.label: Above-the-break three
nodes.definition: A three from the wing or the top, produced by relocation, kick-outs and ball reversals.

nodes.label: Open mid-range
nodes.definition: A clean look from the elbow or short corner: the shot a good defence is willing to concede.

nodes.label: Mismatch created
nodes.definition: A favourable one-on-one (big on small, fast on slow) created by a switch or a cross-match.

nodes.label: Foul drawn
nodes.definition: Contact created by an advantage, resulting in free throws or penalty situation.

nodes.label: Turnover forced
nodes.definition: The defence takes the ball away, usually through pressure, traps or a deflection.

nodes.label: Offensive rebound
nodes.definition: The possession is extended by crashing the glass against a defence that is out of position to box out.

nodes.label: Deflection
nodes.definition: A ball touched in a passing lane, disrupting the timing of the offence.

nodes.label: Switch the ball screen
nodes.definition: Switch everything off the ball screen so the pass to the roller disappears and the action becomes an isolation.

props.vulnerability: The mismatch and the slip
props.rationale: Switching removes the two-on-two advantage by definition: there is no separation to pass into.
key: Requires five switchable defenders, not two
The scram switch must be pre-called to hide the weakest defender

nodes.label: Blitz the ball handler
nodes.definition: Send both defenders at the ball to force it out of the initiator's hands and invite a turnover.

props.vulnerability: The 4-on-3 behind the trap, especially a short-roll passer or a hub big
props.rationale: Two on the ball is only safe if the offence cannot pass on time; the counter is a bet on their processing speed.
key: The back line must rotate 'next man up' on the same beat as the trap
Never blitz a short-roll passer without help on the roll

nodes.label: ICE the side ball screen
nodes.definition: Force the ball handler to the baseline so the sideline becomes an extra defender and the pull-up three disappears.

props.vulnerability: The reject to the middle and the subsequent ball reversal
props.rationale: Taking away the middle takes away the pull-up, the pocket pass and the skip pass in one move.
key: Only viable on the side, never on a middle ball screen
The weak side must be loaded for the kick-out

nodes.label: Short roll against the blitz
nodes.definition: Against a trap, the screener catches at the elbow and plays 4-on-3: shoot it, or hit the corner and the weak-side lift.

props.vulnerability: Defenders committing two to the ball leave three defenders for four players
props.rationale: The blitz creates a numerical disadvantage behind it; a decision-maker at the elbow converts it into an open shot every time.
key: Catch on the move, get your feet to the rim
The read is: is the corner's defender helping? If yes, skip it; if no, shoot or drive

nodes.label: Pull-up three against drop coverage
nodes.definition: When the big sinks, the ball handler simply shoots it off the dribble before help can arrive.

props.vulnerability: The drop concedes the shot to protect the rim
props.rationale: A defence that refuses to contest the ball handler has already lost the shot-quality battle if he can shoot.
key: Screen must be set high enough to give the handler a clean window
Get into the shot before the big's shadow, not after

nodes.label: Pop the screen instead of rolling
nodes.definition: A stretch big pops to the arc after screening, dragging the drop big out of the paint and emptying the lane.

props.vulnerability: The drop big cannot be at the rim and on the popper at the same time
props.rationale: It converts the defence's strength (rim protection) into its weakness (closeout defence).
key: The pop must be to a spot the big is uncomfortable contesting
The ball handler must be willing to hit the popper, not just hunt his own shot

nodes.label: Slip the screen against a switch
nodes.definition: When the defence jumps the switch, the screener abandons the screen early and cuts to the rim before his new defender is set.

props.vulnerability: A pre-emptive switch leaves nobody accountable for the screener for a beat
props.rationale: The switch is a bet on being able to pass off the action; a slip makes the pass-off happen one frame too late.
key: The slip must be sold as a screen until the last instant
Timing: slip when the defender's head turns

nodes.label: Post the mismatch
nodes.definition: After a switch, get the ball to the mismatch on the block immediately, before the defence can scram out of it.

props.vulnerability: Every switch creates a mismatch somewhere on the floor
props.rationale: A guard defending a big on the block is a free basket or a double-team that opens the arc.
key: Attack before the scram switch arrives
If the double comes, the corner and the weak-side lift are open

nodes.label: Step-back isolation against a switch
nodes.definition: When the switch takes away the pass, the initiator separates with a step-back rather than a screen.

props.vulnerability: A slow big switched onto a guard in space is a shot-quality problem
props.rationale: If the defence will not help, the offence does not need to move the ball: it needs one favourable one-on-one.
key: Best used late in the clock, when the defence cannot rotate out of it
Clear the side so the help defender cannot stunt

nodes.label: Switch every off-ball screen
nodes.definition: Against motion offence, deny the cutting lanes by switching all off-ball screens, turning the offence into five isolations.

props.vulnerability: Switching off-ball creates mismatches and slows the defensive rotations
props.rationale: Cutting only works against defenders who are chasing; switching removes the chase.
key: Communication is the cost: every switch is a verbal exchange
Offensive rebounding punishes cross-matched defences

nodes.label: Physicality and nail help against motion
nodes.definition: Disrupt timing by denying the first pass and filling the cutting lanes with bodies, within the freedom-of-movement rule.

props.vulnerability: Over-aggression becomes a foul and opens the backdoor
props.rationale: Motion depends on timing: a cut that arrives half a second late is not a cut.
key: Get through, do not hold: bumps must be momentary
Fill the nail so the basket cut has to end in a contested finish

nodes.label: Occupy the high post against the 2-3
nodes.definition: Station a player at the free-throw line, the 'hole' of the 2-3 zone, where a catch splits the bottom three and forces a choice between the rim and the corners.

props.vulnerability: The free-throw line is the geometric hole of the 2-3 shell
props.rationale: A catch at the middle of the zone makes the two bottom corner defenders choose, and either choice is wrong.
key: The player there must be a passer, not just a scorer
Fill both corners and the short corners so the help cannot cheat

nodes.label: Overload one side of the 2-3
nodes.definition: Put three or four players on one side of the floor so the zone has more attackers than defenders on that side, then skip to the vacated corner.

props.vulnerability: A zone must allocate one defender per area; overloading breaks the allocation
props.rationale: The zone counts heads, not matchups: put more heads in one area than it can cover.
key: Overload the strong side, then reverse to the empty side
The skip pass is the shot, not the drive

nodes.label: Quick ball reversal against the 2-3
nodes.definition: Swing the ball top-to-wing-to-top-to-wing quickly so the shell has to shift twice in one possession; the second shift is always late.

props.vulnerability: A zone moves on the flight of the ball; two quick reversals beat the rotation
props.rationale: Zone defence is a reaction to the ball; make it react twice faster than it can.
key: The reversal must be in the air before the first rotation settles
Attack the 'seams', not the occupied areas

nodes.label: Crash the offensive glass against the 2-3
nodes.definition: Send two or three players to the offensive boards: zone defenders guard areas, not men, so they are often out of position to box out.

props.vulnerability: Zone defenders are responsible for space, not for a body to box out
props.rationale: The structural weakness of any pure zone is finishing the possession with a rebound.
key: Crash from the perimeter, where the zone has no one to block out
Keep one player back for transition defence

nodes.label: Run before the 2-3 can set
nodes.definition: Push the ball in transition so the zone never gets into its shell; a half-set zone is just five players in the wrong places.

props.vulnerability: A zone needs time and a dead ball to organise
props.rationale: The best zone offence is a made basket or a stopped ball: deny them the chance to set up.
key: Rim run to occupy the back line, then the trailing corner three
Early drag screen catches the zone in a cross-match

nodes.label: Middle release and advance pass against the press
nodes.definition: Get the ball to the middle of the floor, then over the top: the press dies when the ball beats the trap line.

props.vulnerability: A trap leaves one player open by definition
props.rationale: Two defenders on the ball means a team-mate is free; find him before the five-second count bites.
key: Sideline safety valve first, middle release second
Do not dribble into the trap: pass out of it before it forms

nodes.label: Sprint back and build a wall
nodes.definition: Against early offence, send three players level with the ball to protect the rim first, then find shooters.

props.vulnerability: Transitions create numbers if the defence retreats behind the ball
props.rationale: Protect the rim first and concede nothing easy: a contested three in semi-transition is a win for the defence.
key: Never retreat behind the ball: get level with it
The deepest defender takes the rim runner; the others find the arc
